theme: IAMB and MMPC against bnlearn, and the discrete networks
build: three pre-release Andrey builds: the standardized grid on the 0.12.0 build (29 October 2026), the unstandardized, d = 200, and discrete-network error grids on the 0.13.0 build (30 October 2026), and the discrete-network fit times on the 0.13.0 build of 31 October 2026 with the faster discrete tests

regimes.linear_gauss_er: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graphs, standardized, d 20/50/100, n 1000/5000, mean degree 2/4; seeds 0-19 attempted, at least 10 per setting run
regimes.linear_gauss_er_unitless: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graphs, not standardized; d 20/50/100, n 1000/5000, mean degree 2/4; seeds 0-19 attempted, 10 to 16 run (CPU budget guard)
regimes.discrete_networks_chisq: discrete published networks asia, child, insurance, alarm, hepar2 (andrey.data.load_dataset), n 1000/5000, seeds 0-19 attempted, 10 to 20 run; Andrey chisq/gsq against bnlearn x2-adf/mi-adf, BDeu (iss 1) for the hybrids
regimes.discrete_networks_gsq: discrete published networks asia, child, insurance, alarm, hepar2 (andrey.data.load_dataset), n 1000/5000, seeds 0-19 attempted, 10 to 20 run; Andrey chisq/gsq against bnlearn x2-adf/mi-adf, BDeu (iss 1) for the hybrids
regimes.linear_gauss_er_d200: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graphs, standardized, d 200, n 1000/5000, mean degree 2/4, the blanket methods whose d=100 fits all finished; seeds 0-9

verdict_rule: D = error(Andrey) - error(bnlearn) per dataset on the datasets both finished; a setting with at least 10 paired datasets is worse when the paired 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; fewer than 10 pairs is reported, not judged; a setting that is worse is rerun once on fresh seeds (a replication, in the row) and counts as worse only if the rerun's own interval also lies entirely above 0
fit_protocol: one fit at a time on 1 core, a 600 s wall cap per fit, 1 untimed warm-up fit except at n=5000, mean degree 4, d>=50 (none), 1 timed fit; a capped fit is a timeout, counted as coverage and never scored. Continuous lanes: Fisher-z tests at alpha 0.05 (bnlearn test zf). Discrete-network lanes: chi-square or G-square tests at alpha 0.05 (bnlearn x2-adf or mi-adf), with fit times re-measured on the build with the faster discrete tests, the same datasets and seeds, one core, and the same warm-up rule; the graphs of that build equal the campaign's, so the errors are the campaign's
error_metric: each entry's own, in its error_metric: the SHD of the output against its own true graph (the moral graph, the skeleton, or the CPDAG), as the median over the paired datasets (the _mean fields hold the means)
complete_definition: true when every setting has at least 10 paired datasets (both packages finished); a setting with fewer is listed in incomplete, its timeouts counted in the timeout columns and never scored
seeds_note: seeds is the number of datasets attempted per setting: 10 to 20 of the 20 planned in the standardized grid, 10 to 16 of 20 in the unstandardized grid (the CPU budget guard skipped the rest before they ran), and 10 of 10 at 200 variables

methods.note: The setting with 50 variables, 5,000 rows, and mean degree 2 is worse (D +0.50 [+0.05, +1.05]); 16 of its 20 graphs are identical. Most of the gap, +7 pairs of the +10 over its 20 datasets, sits in 2 datasets whose skeletons differ, and the skeleton difference starts at one node's first grow step, where the p-values of several candidates underflow to exactly 0 in bnlearn, which takes the first column among them. Andrey takes the candidate with the strongest test statistic, the association measure of Tsamardinos, Aliferis, and Statnikov (2003). bnlearn's choice, applied in Andrey's search, reproduces bnlearn's skeleton in all 4 traced datasets. The other +3 are orientation differences in 2 datasets with equal skeletons: Meek's rules on a cyclic partially directed graph, and a collider that bnlearn skips for closing a directed cycle.

methods.note: The skeleton at 200 variables, 5,000 rows, and mean degree 2 is worse (D +1.60 [+0.10, +3.10] on seeds 0-9 and +2.70 [+1.20, +4.40] on seeds 20-29). At this size MMPC's forward step often faces candidates whose dependence is too strong to rank by p-value, and Andrey admits the one with the strongest test statistic, the association measure of Tsamardinos, Brown, and Aliferis (2006), which is a true neighbor in 2,376 of 2,384 first picks (99.7%); the first column, bnlearn's pick, is one in 49%. The extra errors are false edges between unrelated pairs whose statistic is just past the cutoff (z 2.0 to 3.1, the cutoff is 1.96); an arbitrary pick happens to admit a strongly correlated non-neighbor that removes some of them. Strongest-first keeps 44 such edges that the other order removes, about 2 per graph.

methods.note: The moral graph of hepar2 at 5,000 rows is worse on both runs (D +5.81 [+1.81, +9.63] on seeds 0-19 and +10.30 [+5.20, +15.20] on seeds 20-29). The two packages run different discrete tests: Andrey's chi-square test is calibrated by the exact permutation mean of the statistic as its degrees of freedom (Tsamardinos and Borboudakis 2010), and bnlearn's x2-adf adjusts the degrees of freedom by a rule for sparse tables. Their graphs are not equal on any of the 3,183 datasets of child, insurance, alarm, and hepar2 (595 of 790 on asia), and the two tests agree on 97.7% of random triples.
